rv.q: The Hungry Ghost as a production simply gets everything right.
She makes an already striking play about the push and pull between cultural tradition and independence all the more compelling.
For a first-time playwright, The Hungry Ghost is a confident and wonderfully original piece of writing, and one that leaves its audience hungry for whatever Yew serves up next.
The Hungry Ghost is a feat of excellence, expertly blending modernity and Chinese mythology to create a touching and well-executed piece.
It's enjoyable and worth seeing – expect to laugh a lot – but it isn't flawless.
It’s warm, hilariously funny and heartfelt.
For horror with real heart, The Hungry Ghost is the perfect addition to your spooky season lineup this October.

This is an eye-popping, delightfully delirious debut work. Blisteringly funny but also deeply moving, there is a lot to like on The Hungry Ghost's menu, with the play, like a meal for Girl, not to be missed.
Everything about The Hungry Ghost feels exciting.
Ailin Conant’s 100-miles-per-hour direction makes this an utter thrill to watch, and gives weight to those rare moments of silence.

The Hungry Ghost is a play that is culturally rich and fast-paced, almost to the point of wanting it to slow down for a moment. But it's highly imaginative and successfully sustains its ideas, and you won't see anything else quite like it.
The Ghost's departure from Girl leaves a sense of a story well rounded and well told, though a little more time with the Ghost's life before she became a ghost might have been even more satisfying.
The Hungry Ghost is a true example of why to go to the theatre: with its unique story and excellent production, its compelling from start to finish and leaves you hungry for more.

cn.t: Mei Leng Yew's debut play earns widespread acclaim for its inventive blend of Chinese mythology and modern romance, with critics praising Mei Mac's outstanding performance and the show's skillful balance of humor, horror, and heartfelt cultural storytelling.
